question.prompt: For a set of four distinct lines in a plane, there are exactly \(N\) distinct points that lie on two or more of the lines. What is the sum of all possible values of \(N?\)

solutions.title: Classify parallel and concurrent lines
solutions.explanation:
Several pairs of lines can share one intersection point. To account for this, first separate arrangements according to whether at least three lines pass through a common point.

If all four lines pass through one point, then \(N=1\).

If exactly three lines pass through a point \(P\), the fourth line does not pass through \(P\). The three lines through \(P\) have different directions, so the fourth can be parallel to at most one of them.

- If it is parallel to one, it meets the other two at two distinct points outside \(P\), giving \(N=1+2=3\).
- If it is parallel to none, it creates three distinct new intersections, giving \(N=1+3=4\).

It remains to consider arrangements with no three lines passing through one point. Here every intersecting pair gives a different point. Classify these arrangements by the largest number of mutually parallel lines:

- Four parallel lines give \(N=0\).
- Exactly three parallel lines are crossed by the fourth at three distinct points, giving \(N=3\).
- If the largest parallel group has two lines, the other two lines each cross both of them, producing four points. If those other two lines are parallel to each other, \(N=4\). Otherwise, their intersection adds one more point, so \(N=5\).
- If there are no parallel lines, every pair intersects. There are \(\binom42=6\) pairs, giving \(N=6\).

These cases cover every arrangement. Each can be realized by drawing the indicated parallel or concurrent lines and avoiding any additional triple intersections. Thus the distinct possible values are
\[
0,1,3,4,5,6.
\]
Counting each value once, their sum is
\[
0+1+3+4+5+6=\boxed{19}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
